newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Poor earnings likely to hit Manila shares again.
newsitem.headline: Poor earnings likely to hit Manila shares again.

text.p: Disappointing company profits are likely to knock Philippine shares again on Wednesday after they fell the previous day to their lowest in over two years, analysts said.
The main stock market index on Tuesday plunged 128.87 points at 2,708.44, a drop of more than 20 percent from record highs in early February.
"We are still in murky waters. There is still some room for weakness although at this level, the market has started to become oversold," said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities.
"The results of San Miguel were disappointing and so was Meralco. Those two alone could carry sentiment," said Raul Ruiz, research head at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Both index heavyweights, food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp and Manila Electric Co reported their first quarter earnings after the trading session ended on Tuesday.
Asian Capital Equities recommended a short-term sell on San Miguel.
Angping & Associates analyst Alexis Cabel said the market wsa likely to shrug off the Dow's overnight advance, noting PLDT's American Depositary Receipt fell by $1 5/8 to $56 5/8.
Analysts said some investors were worried that economic growth might not be as strong as previously hoped.

"Meralco (Manila Electric Co) is the best GDP gauge and if it reported a slowdown then a lot of people would naturally assume that there may be some slowdown in the economy," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital Inc.
Meralco earlier announced sales growth for the first quarter well below market expectations.

"If investments have to be made, we continue to advise investors to focus on consumer-related stocks where both market sentiment and corporate fundamentals are strong," said BPI Securities analyst Bernadette Tamayo.
Traders said the market may test support at 2,600 to 2,650 points.
